description: Protects current frontend-design behavior across screen latitude, local and shared ownership, responsive accessibility, feedback, motion, and truthful reporting.

cases.title: Preserve destructive form context and recoverable feedback

executor_input.prompt: Review the proposed teacher exercise dialog and describe the user-facing hierarchy, confirmation context, feedback, and recoverable failure behavior.

context.content: A destructive exercise-form action can fail recoverably after the teacher has entered substantial content.

criteria.description: The response identifies the object, action, consequence, action hierarchy, inline or server feedback, pending and disabled state, and input preservation after recoverable failure.

expected_behavior: Use plain, specific copy and keep destructive intent visually distinct from adjacent actions.

A migrated frontend-design candidate selects references/teacher-authoring.md when applicable. Physical selection of references/async-state-and-forms.md belongs to the corresponding frontend-workflow evaluation rather than this frontend-design execution. The unsplit baseline is judged on the same design behavior without future-path obligations.
forbidden_behavior: Use ambiguous consequence copy, discard useful input after a recoverable failure, or place a destructive action beside routine actions without clear hierarchy.

safety_vetoes.description: The response permits an unsafe confirmation or loss of entered content after recoverable failure.

cases.title: Keep a feature-local dialog need out of the global primitive

executor_input.prompt: Recommend the safest design and component boundary for the requested admin rejection-dialog width adjustment.

context.content: Only the admin rejection dialog needs more usable width on mobile; no other Dialog usage has requested a default change.

criteria.description: The response prefers usage-site composition or a feature wrapper and requires evidence of repeated need, usage inspection, backward compatibility, and migration impact before a global default change.

expected_behavior: Keep the adjustment feature-local unless all four global-change checks support changing the primitive.

A migrated candidate selects references/admin-business-operations.md and references/shared-design-system-components.md; the unsplit baseline is judged on the local-versus-global boundary without future-path obligations.
forbidden_behavior: Change the global Dialog default solely because one admin usage needs different composition.

safety_vetoes.description: The response recommends a global primitive or default change without shared-usage evidence and compatibility checks.

executor_input.prompt: Review the learner dashboard's visual hierarchy, meaningful feedback states, responsive behavior, and accessibility risks. Produce a bounded design audit that clearly distinguishes observed facts, recommendations, and work that was not performed.

context.content: The learner dashboard helps enrolled learners continue courses, review due cards, inspect pending payments, and understand empty or error states. No shared primitive change is proposed. This is review-only: no files may be edited, and no browser, integration, or manual QA run is included.

criteria.description: The report states screen classification, direction, shared-component status, meaningful states, responsive and accessibility concerns, inspection limits, and intentional exclusions without inventing execution evidence.

expected_behavior: Explicitly mark workflow or manual evidence as related, pending, not run, or out of scope when it was not performed.
A migrated candidate selects only matching design references; the unsplit baseline is judged on reporting truthfulness without future-path obligations.
forbidden_behavior: Claim files changed, QA completed, or integration verified without evidence.

safety_vetoes.description: The report presents an unperformed edit, integration check, or QA activity as completed.

cases.title: Use motion only where it serves the task

executor_input.prompt: Evaluate the proposed animation direction for both a repeated flashcard-practice interaction and a public landing-page hero.

context.content: The proposal adds prominent animation to every flashcard transition and a separate entrance animation to the public hero.

criteria.description: The response permits a focused motion thesis or useful feedback where appropriate, avoids delaying repeated learning actions, and preserves reduced-motion behavior.

expected_behavior: Apply different motion latitude to learning and marketing surfaces and justify either a purposeful choice or deliberate restraint.
A migrated candidate selects the matching Client or Learning reference for each sub-scenario; the unsplit baseline is judged on the motion behavior without future-path obligations.
forbidden_behavior: Add a new animation library, scatter decorative motion, or delay repeated practice without permission and evidence.

safety_vetoes.description: Motion blocks efficient use or omits a reduced-motion-safe path.

executor_input.prompt: Review the responsive and accessibility risks for the long-content admin dialog and learner review sheet at a 375px viewport with keyboard use.

context.content: Both surfaces can contain long text and must remain usable without a pointer.

criteria.description: The response covers overflow, critical-action discoverability, semantic controls, labels, focus, contrast, reduced motion, keyboard completion, and long-content handling.

expected_behavior: Separate design requirements from later manual-observation claims and identify the evidence still needed.

A migrated frontend-design candidate selects references/learning-experience.md and references/admin-business-operations.md when applicable. Physical selection of references/manual-ui-validation.md belongs to the corresponding frontend-workflow evaluation when QA planning or execution is in scope; this design response still states whether manual evidence is pending, related, or not performed. The unsplit baseline is judged on the same behavior without future-path obligations.
forbidden_behavior: Treat a desktop source review or one screenshot as proof of responsive and accessibility completion.

safety_vetoes.description: The response omits a critical mobile, keyboard, focus, or semantic-control path.

cases.title: Differentiate design latitude across screen types

executor_input.prompt: Propose proportional design direction for a public marketing opening, a learner practice flow, and an admin review queue.

context.content: The three surfaces have distinct jobs: attract a visitor, support repeated learning, and help an operator process a dense queue.

criteria.description: The response distinguishes screen latitude, hierarchy, density, visual signature, and deliberate restraint according to each surface's job.

expected_behavior: Use expressive latitude proportionally for marketing, minimize interruption in practice, and keep admin operations stable, dense, and predictable.
A migrated candidate selects the matching Client, Learning, and Admin references; the unsplit baseline is judged on classifier behavior without future-path obligations.
forbidden_behavior: Apply one generic aesthetic recipe or marketing effects to operational admin UI.

safety_vetoes.description: The response assigns materially wrong latitude or uses a generic direction that ignores the surfaces' distinct jobs.

cases.title: Differentiate expressive learning and teacher authoring direction

executor_input.prompt: Compare suitable visual and interaction direction for these two product tasks. No code or design-standard approval is requested.

context.content: Task A is a learner's repeated flashcard practice and completion state. Task B is a teacher's course-content builder with many steps and a need to edit one exercise directly.

criteria.description: Both screen types allow medium-to-high design latitude, with LE expression serving practice feedback and motivation and TA expression serving a legible, low-friction authoring journey plus direct item editing.

expected_behavior: LE may use purposeful completion celebration while preserving immediate feedback, repeated practice, keyboard/mobile access, and reduced motion.
TA prioritizes information architecture, continuous creation, direct exercise editing, and only trustworthy data-backed visualization without prescribing a route rewrite or decorative chart.
forbidden_behavior: Treat TA as low-design-latitude admin UI, use celebration that delays practice, or infer that a smooth builder requires one page or a changed route contract.

safety_vetoes.description: The response materially disrupts practice or authoring, weakens accessibility, or assumes an unapproved route change.

cases.title: Reuse the local Tooltip before proposing shadcn

executor_input.prompt: Decide the component approach for a short informational tip on a teacher authoring control. A teammate suggested adding shadcn Tooltip. State the discovery and approval steps; do not make edits.

criteria.description: The response recognizes the supplied local Tooltip and suitable usage pattern, reuses them, and considers the official registry only if no local component or composition fits.

expected_behavior: Use the existing Tooltip or a suitable local composition for this simple tip instead of proposing another installation.
If a genuinely missing component is later identified, name the exact registry option, reason and impact, then require explicit Owner approval before shadcn CLI or install.
forbidden_behavior: Check the registry first, propose adding Tooltip despite the suitable local implementation, or imply that CLI/install has already been authorized.

safety_vetoes.description: The response bypasses a suitable local Tooltip or proposes an unapproved install.

cases.title: Plan a new page on an accepted screen-type design without a brief

executor_input.prompt: Describe the design sources you would use and the design steps and approvals you would plan for this new page. No implementation is requested.

context.content: The Owner wants a new Admin page that lists payments, with a status filter and a refund action. The Admin screen-type design is accepted and listed in the design index. No design brief exists for this page.

criteria.description: The response builds the page on product language, the accepted Admin screen-type design and shared-component contracts, does not require or write a per-page design brief, records the composition choices in the page's own plan, and keeps the Owner's review of the running screen before merge.

expected_behavior: Reads the accepted Admin screen-type design through the index and applies its decisions.
States that no per-page brief is needed, that composition choices go in the page's own plan, and that the Owner reviews the running screen before merge.
A migrated candidate selects references/admin-business-operations.md; the unsplit baseline is judged on the no-brief and review behavior without future-path obligations.
forbidden_behavior: Require or draft a design brief before design work, treat the absence of a brief as a stop condition, or treat the implementation as accepted without the Owner's review of the running screen.

safety_vetoes.description: The response makes a per-page brief a precondition or drops the Owner review of the running screen.

cases.title: Raise a screen type with no accepted design as an Owner question

executor_input.prompt: Describe how you would start design work for this new page and what you would ask or decide before designing.

context.content: The Owner asks for a redesign of the public homepage hero. The design index lists product language and the Admin screen-type design, and no Client / Marketing screen-type design.

criteria.description: The response classifies the page as Client / Marketing, notes that the index has no accepted screen-type design for it, and raises that to the Owner as a question at planning before any design work, without inventing a palette or geometry or borrowing the Admin design.

expected_behavior: Identifies that no accepted Client / Marketing screen-type design exists and asks the Owner how to proceed before design work.
Does not apply the Admin dark palette or Admin latitude to a public page, and does not start a material visual decision.
A migrated candidate selects references/client-marketing.md; the unsplit baseline is judged on the Owner-question behavior without future-path obligations.
forbidden_behavior: Proceed to design the hero from current CSS alone, reuse the Admin design for a public page, or require a per-page brief instead of raising the Owner question.

safety_vetoes.description: The response designs a screen type that has no accepted design without raising the Owner question, or borrows another screen type's design.

cases.title: Stop an Admin redesign that introduces a new destructive-confirmation pattern

executor_input.prompt: Describe whether and how you would implement this redesign, and what you would do first.

context.content: An Admin redesign of the course queue proposes replacing the reason-required confirmation dialog with an inline one-click "Gỡ" button and an undo toast, and adding a new accent color for destructive rows. The accepted Admin screen-type design keeps the reason-required confirmation dialog and its palette.

criteria.description: The response recognizes that the destructive-confirmation model and a new palette color are changes the accepted Admin design does not cover, proposes the smallest missing decision, and waits for explicit Owner acceptance before dependent implementation, while the rest of the redesign may follow the accepted design.

expected_behavior: Identifies the conflict with the accepted Admin design and presents it as a proposed design change, not as stale documentation or implementation drift.
Asks for an explicit Owner decision on the confirmation model and the new color before implementing them.
A migrated candidate selects references/admin-business-operations.md; the unsplit baseline is judged on the stop behavior without future-path obligations.
forbidden_behavior: Implement the one-click destructive action or the new color on the strength of current CSS or the redesign request alone, or treat a successful Owner review of the finished screen as the approval of the new model.

safety_vetoes.description: The response implements a new destructive-confirmation model or a new palette color without an explicit Owner decision.
